tiers.name: Part I: Key News & Developments
tiers.description: Macro economy, politics, social security, international relations, industry and key client movements in Paraguay

tiers.name: Part II: Analysis & Recommendations
tiers.description: Enterprise impact assessment and China-specific strategic recommendations

events.title: BCP intervenes in the FX market for the first time in 2026 as the dollar spikes (2026-11-11)
events.summary: The Central Bank sold USD 14.7 million on Thursday 5 November and USD 12.7 million on Friday 6 November, its first currency intervention of 2026, to damp a spike in the dollar during the impeachment of Santiago Peña. The dollar touched G. 6,600 during the Ueno Bank run and then retreated to about G. 6,200-6,300; the BCP planilla of Friday 13 November fixed the reference rate at G. 6,215.89 per dollar, up roughly 4.5% from G. 5,944.76 on 30 October. The move marks a break with a year in which the BCP had intervened only to slow the guaraní's appreciation. The Senate also requested a report on the exchange-rate impact of the Ueno resolution and on the criteria for intervention.

events.title: Senate confirms Jorge Schreiner as BCP president and whistleblower Rivarola to the board (2026-11-09)
events.summary: In an extraordinary session the Senate approved Jorge Luis Schreiner Marengo as president of the Central Bank by 31 votes to 1 with 1 abstention, and Fernando Javier Rivarola Angulo as a full board member by 33 votes to nil. Schreiner, a former head of the securities regulator CNV and BCP board member, replaces Carlos Carvallo, who resigned after the Ueno Bank collapse; Rivarola is the former supervision manager who flagged Ueno's irregularities. Schreiner said his priority is to restore the BCP's credibility and that he will use Article 50 of Law 489/95 to intervene against abrupt, non-fundamental currency moves, including buying dollars if the guaraní overshoots. The appointments were proposed by President Pedro Alliana.

events.title: Exports top USD 17.8bn through October as the soy complex sets a record (2026-11-11)
events.summary: Paraguayan exports reached USD 17,815.6 million between January and October, up 25% year-on-year, producing a trade surplus of USD 668.6 million after a deficit of about USD 720 million in the same period of 2025. The soy complex generated USD 6,624 million, almost double the USD 3,330 million of 2025, on 8.3 million tonnes of grain, 595,298 tonnes of oil, 2.09 million tonnes of pellets and 31,172 tonnes of biodiesel. The 2025/26 harvest hit a record 12.6 million tonnes. Argentina took 85-87% of grain exports and Brazil about 11%. The BCP put grain soy alone at USD 3,316.9 million, up 45.7% in value and 35.7% in volume. The record is the strongest counterweight to the confidence shock from the banking crisis.

events.title: BCP has returned USD 335-355m to 1.7m Ueno depositors, but the guarantee fund covers only 27% (2026-11-11)
events.summary: By 10-11 November the BCP had returned about USD 335-355 million to between 1.7 and 1.78 million Ueno Bank depositors, roughly 93-97% of those eligible in the first phase, under an emergency law that sped up payouts of up to 40 minimum wages (about USD 19,500). Ueno held USD 2.8-2.84 billion in deposits, 71% private and the rest public entities, mainly the IPS pension institute. The Deposit Guarantee Fund covers up to 75 minimum wages, about G. 228.3 million (USD 37,000-38,300) per depositor, and expects to pay about USD 740 million, only 27% of total deposits. The remainder depends on asset sales and liquidation, with pension funds given priority. The BCP insists the case is idiosyncratic and not systemic.

events.title: Alliana takes office after the Senate removes Peña over the Ueno Bank collapse (2026-11-06)
events.summary: Vice-President Pedro Alliana became president on 6 November after the Senate convicted Santiago Peña in an impeachment trial with 44 votes, one day after the Chamber of Deputies approved the charges 78-0. Peña had announced his resignation on 5 November, but a joint congressional session lost quorum when Colorado legislators walked out, and the opposition pressed ahead to strip him of lifetime Senate privileges. The charges centred on conflicts of interest from his former shareholding in the Ueno holding group, regulatory manipulation and the loss of pension funds. The courts ordered Peña held under house arrest and detained eight Ueno executives, including former bank president Juan Manuel Gustale and Federico Miguel Vázquez Villasanti. Alliana, a Colorado leader, will serve until August 2028.

events.title: Alliana asks every minister to resign and reshuffles the cabinet and military command (2026-11-09)
events.summary: On his first working Monday Alliana instructed new chief of staff Rolando de Barros Barreto to ask all ministers, executive secretaries and heads of public entities to place their posts at his disposal, warning that 'no job is guaranteed.' He named Ariel Martínez at the Interior Ministry, Juan Carlos Baruja at Public Works (MOPC), Juan Pablo Cosp as interim head of MITIC after removing Gustavo Villate, Víctor González Bedoya at environment agency MADES and Eduardo González Báez as presidential legal adviser. He ratified Óscar Lovera at the Treasury, Marco Riquelme at Industry, Rubén Ramírez Lezcano at Foreign Affairs and Isaías Fretes at Health. General Manuel Rodríguez Sosa was named commander of the armed forces, with new interim chiefs for the army, air force and military cabinet. More changes are expected.

events.title: Alliana sends Congress a bill to place Ueno-linked companies under temporary state administration (2026-11-12)
events.summary: The executive sent Congress a bill to keep companies linked to the collapsed Ueno Bank operating and protect jobs. It would appoint a temporary administrator for eight months, remove incumbent directors and managers, and create a supervisory council with the Treasury, Industry and Labour ministries. The state would not assume the companies' debts and the measure would exclude firms under criminal investigation or in the hands of the asset-seizure agency Senabico; asset transfers, dividends and payments to shareholders would be restricted. Officials say the aim is to preserve more than 5,000 jobs. The industrial union UIP warned there is 'no margin for error' and urged spending discipline rather than tax increases, while the MIC, Treasury and bankers' association Asoban set up a working group on working-capital finance for November and December.

events.title: Teachers launch an indefinite national strike over Ueno-hit pension funds (2026-11-09)
events.summary: Public-school teachers began an indefinite national strike on 9 November, called by the FEP, UNE-SN, OTEP-Auténtica, OTEP-SN and the school directors' union SINADI, with the main rally at the Plaza de Armas facing Congress. They demand the return of about USD 60 million of Caja Fiscal money and USD 350 million of IPS pension funds caught in Ueno Bank, state guarantees for pensions, a law shielding the two funds, an 8% salary rise and more education spending in the 2027 budget. Classes were suspended nationwide and the Hambre Cero school-meals programme was paused in Asunción, Central, Presidente Hayes and San Pedro. The government opened talks the same day and later agreed to lift the salary floor from 5% to 8%, clear pending retirements and extend the school day by 30 minutes in exchange for no pay deductions.

events.title: Paraguay asks Argentina, Luxembourg and the US to trace Ueno Bank assets (2026-11-10)
events.summary: The Paraguayan government confirmed it asked Argentina, Luxembourg and the United States for judicial cooperation to trace possible Ueno Bank funds and assets abroad. Prosecutors have detained eight executives, including former bank president Juan Manuel Gustale and controlling shareholder Federico Miguel Vázquez Villasanti, and imposed preventive embargoes of USD 70 million and G. 1.62 trillion. The IPS says USD 328-380 million of pension money was exposed, putting benefits for about 32,000 retirees at risk, and has filed a criminal complaint. Public-sector deposits in the bank are estimated at USD 850-869 million, about 29% of deposits at June. The case has become a test of Paraguay's ability to recover assets across borders.

events.title: Police bring forward the year-end 'Año Paha' operation with 5,900 officers in the capital region (2026-11-11)
events.summary: After a run of armed robberies and an attempted ATM break-in in San Lorenzo, the National Police brought forward its year-end 'Año Paha' security operation. It deploys about 2,347 officers in Asunción and 3,550 in Central department, plus tactical units with long weapons, the Lima 40 group, motorcycles, patrols and investigators. Banks, shopping areas, ATMs and residential neighbourhoods are prioritised, with coverage extended to Alto Paraná (especially Ciudad del Este), Amambay, Canindeyú, Curuguaty and Saltos del Guairá. The police offer free escorts for cash transfers, including the December bonus, and 5,000 new officers are due to graduate on 18 December. Officials link the early deployment to the heightened risk during the banking crisis.

events.title: Shootout in Ciudad del Este leaves one suspect dead and another wounded (2026-11-11)
events.summary: An off-duty police officer foiled a motorcycle robbery in Ciudad del Este on 11 November, pursued the suspects and exchanged gunfire, killing one attacker and wounding another. Both suspects had criminal records. The incident came amid reports of an insecurity wave in Alto Paraná, with vehicle thefts and robberies in Ciudad del Este, Minga Guazú, Presidente Franco and Hernandarias, and follows the early launch of the Año Paha operation. Business groups in the triple-border area have long complained about the cost of private security and the impact of crime on retail and logistics; the new Interior Minister, Ariel Martínez, has promised a harder line and tighter coordination with the Public Ministry.

events.title: Alliana keeps Peña's foreign policy and says US, Israel and Taiwan ties remain intact (2026-11-08)
events.summary: President Alliana will maintain Santiago Peña's foreign policy and reaffirm alliances with the United States, Israel and Taiwan, according to government officials quoted after the transition. Taiwan, Paraguay's only diplomatic ally in South America, said on 6 November that the change of government would not affect relations, and Asunción signalled that ties with Washington, Jerusalem and Taipei remain intact. The continuity covers the SOFA status-of-forces agreement signed in March 2026, participation in the US-led 'Shield of the Americas' security initiative and cooperation against transnational crime. A planned meeting between Peña and Donald Trump on 14 November was left in doubt; officials said it could be held by videoconference with Alliana. Beijing sanctioned MITIC minister Gustavo Villate in October over his Taiwan support.

events.title: Alliana suspends his official trip to Taiwan to focus on the domestic crisis (2026-11-09)
events.summary: Chief of staff Rolando de Barros Barreto confirmed that Alliana suspended his official visit to Taiwan, scheduled for 24 November with a meeting with President Lai Ching-te, to prioritise the domestic agenda. 'He is not one to travel much; his priority is here in the country now,' the official said. The decision distances Alliana from Peña, who was criticised for more than 70 trips, and follows a presidential inauguration speech that did not mention Taiwan. Taipei said the relationship is unaffected, but the episode has revived debate over Paraguay's diplomatic recognition. At least 19 Paraguayan legislators have visited China since late 2023, and a pragmatic, Beijing-leaning faction of the Colorado Party is pressing to open trade ties, though no immediate switch is expected.

events.title: Lula congratulates Alliana and invites him to Brasilia as Itaipú Annex C tops the agenda (2026-11-07)
events.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, re-elected in October, congratulated Pedro Alliana and invited him to Brasilia to review the bilateral agenda and give 'renewed impetus' to relations; Alliana said he expects a 'very fruitful' relationship. The central issue is the revision of Annex C of the Itaipú Treaty: the dam's debt was paid off in February 2023 and the review was due by December 2024, but no agreement was reached. The current tariff of USD 19.28 per kW runs to the end of 2026; Paraguay resists a sharp cut because it wants the revenue for infrastructure and social programmes, while Brazil opposes an increase for regulated consumers. The new ANDE head, Félix Sosa, called the review a 'fundamental strategic priority' and Alliana plans to travel to Brasilia before the end of 2026.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: Contraloría recommends revoking Nubicom's 5G licence as Conatel opens a sumario (2026-11-09)
events.summary: The Comptroller General recommended that Conatel evaluate extinguishing Nubicom Paraguay's 5G licence, awarded by Resolution 2635/2025, after finding it could not prove the first-year rollout plan. Conatel had already opened an administrative sumario (Resolution 2816/2026) after Argentine shareholder Nubicom SRL notified an unauthorised transfer of shares on 5-6 November and failed to identify the buyer, leaving the regulator unsure who controls the licensee. Press reports link Nubicom to the Grupo Vázquez and Ueno Bank; Conatel transferred G. 70 billion to Ueno in October (G. 50 billion from Interfisa on 13 October and G. 20 billion from BNF on 15 October) and Ueno issued a USD 75,000 bid bond for the licence. Conatel says Nubicom met the initial build with 34 radio bases inspected, but has only two subscribers.

events.title: ANDE will let crypto-mining contracts expire in 2027 and redirect Itaipú surplus to AI data centres (2026-11-13)
events.summary: ANDE says all special electricity contracts for crypto miners will expire on 31 December 2027 and will not be extended. Miners contracted about 944 MW until April, close to 13% of Paraguay's Itaipú share, and generated about USD 350 million of revenue in 2026. The surplus is being redirected to AI data centres: Kuntur, linked to Araico and the USD 12 billion Iguazú AI City project, won a 15-year contract for up to 286 MW, starting with 6 MW on 1 December 2026 and scaling to 286 MW by 2029, at a reported tariff of USD 48.91-56.39 per MWh. Crusoe Energy and Araico plan an initial 106 MW with an option to expand to about 280 MW, with first facilities in mid-2027. HIVE, which has about 77% of its mining capacity in Paraguay, also loses its 200 MW and 100 MW contracts at end-2027. National demand rose 17.9% in the first eight months of 2026.

events.title: Paraguay Business Week opens in Ciudad del Este with 260 stands and USD 600m target (2026-11-12)
events.summary: The largest integrated trade fair in Paraguay opened in Ciudad del Este, combining the 17th Paraguay-Brazil Expo, the 10th Expo Maquila, the Alto Paraná Forum Invest and Plaza MiPYMEs. It has 260 stands, more than 300 exhibitors and about 2,000 business meetings, with organisers expecting more than USD 600 million in deals and 12,000 visitors. The Paraguay-Brazil chamber of commerce organised the event with support from the Industry Ministry through Rediex. Bilateral trade reached USD 6,700 million between January and October, up 8% year-on-year, but about 320 Brazilian companies with Paraguayan plants, 90 of them in textiles, are watching credit and payment conditions cautiously after the Ueno crisis.

events.title: Alliana suspends power cuts until 31 December and freezes electricity tariffs for a year (2026-11-13)
events.summary: President Alliana suspended electricity cut-offs for non-payment until 31 December for low- and medium-voltage users and allowed debts to be paid in up to 24 interest-free instalments without penalties. He also said the electricity tariff will not rise for at least a year. The measures are aimed at households and small firms hit by the Ueno Bank crisis and the sudden depreciation of the guaraní, and they add to fiscal pressure on ANDE at a time when demand is growing 17.9% and the government is negotiating the Itaipú Annex C tariff with Brazil. Analysts warn that freezing tariffs while costs rise shifts the burden to the utility's balance sheet and may delay needed grid investment.

events.title: Millicom (Tigo) reports USD 175m Paraguay service revenue and a 54.8% EBITDA margin in Q3 (2026-11-05)
events.summary: Millicom's third-quarter results, published on 5 November, show Paraguay service revenue of USD 175 million, up 3.6% organically year-on-year on postpaid growth, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 101 million, up 11% organically, for a 54.8% margin, one of the highest in the group. At group level service revenue was about USD 2.1 billion (+5.4% organic), adjusted EBITDA a record USD 1.09 billion (+7.7%) at a 48% margin, and equity free cash flow USD 316 million, keeping the full-year guidance near USD 1.1 billion. Leverage fell to 2.53x. Paraguay is grouped with Guatemala, Panama and Ecuador as moderate-growth, high-margin markets. Tigo holds 100 MHz of 2.3 GHz spectrum and must launch commercial 5G by February 2027.

events.title: Telecom Argentina: Personal's Paraguay revenue rises 8.3% in real terms in Q3 (2026-11-12)
events.summary: Telecom Argentina, which operates in Paraguay through Núcleo S.A. under the Personal brand, reported third-quarter mobile service revenue in Paraguay of P. 66,324 million, up 8.3% in real terms year-on-year, and P. 191,752 million for the first nine months, up 16.7% in real terms. The group posted a net loss of P. 56,615 million in the quarter but a net profit of P. 862,959 million for the nine months. TV subscribers across Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay reached 3.6 million, up 4.3%. Núcleo won 5G lots I and J in the 3.7-3.8 GHz band for USD 1 million in July, of which USD 0.7 million has been paid, and must start commercial 5G by February 2027. Personal also plans to launch 5G standalone commercially.

events.title: Claro remains the only live 5G network as Tigo and Personal race the February 2027 deadline (2026-11-12)
events.summary: Claro, which won 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band in the first auction and launched commercially in late 2025, remains the only operator with live 5G in Paraguay, covering 27 cities in 10 departments and more than 3 million people with a USD 35 million five-year plan and more than 100 sites expected by the end of 2026. Tigo and Personal, which won 100 MHz each in the August 2026 second auction, have 180 days from notification to start commercial service, a deadline that falls in February 2027, and must deploy at least 100 radio bases each in four years, 10 of them for state entities within two years. Their projects foresee 250-500 sites and about USD 79-80 million of investment. Neither had launched commercially as of mid-November.

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business
sections.impact_analysis: 🔴 Paraguay has moved from a macro story to a solvency-and-governance story. The resolution of Ueno Bank froze about USD 2.8 billion of deposits, including USD 328-380 million of IPS pension money and about USD 60 million of Caja Fiscal funds, and triggered the removal of President Peña, a new government, a new BCP board and the first FX intervention of 2026. The guaraní swung from G. 5,945 on 30 October to G. 6,600 intraday before settling at G. 6,215.89 on the 13 November planilla, a depreciation of roughly 4.5% in two weeks that reverses part of the 11% year-to-date appreciation. The macro fundamentals remain strong: record exports of USD 17.8 billion through October, a USD 668.6 million trade surplus, 1.7% inflation and a 5.0% growth forecast. But confidence is now the binding constraint. For business: (1) FX volatility is the first-order risk, with a realistic range of G. 6,000-6,600 through year-end; (2) bank counterparty risk is elevated, and the deposit guarantee covers only about 27% of Ueno's deposits; (3) the state's temporary administration of Ueno-linked firms may disrupt suppliers, tenants and service contracts; (4) fiscal pressure, with a 2.0%-of-GDP deficit to September and a 3.2% forecast, limits room for tax relief; (5) the February 2027 5G deadline and ANDE's pivot to AI data centres create capex opportunities but also regulatory uncertainty; (6) the new government is reviewing contracts and reshuffling ministries, so public tenders will slip.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis: 🟡 Chinese enterprises should treat the next quarter as a liquidity and contract-risk exercise. (1) Treasury: move idle guaraní balances to top-tier banks or into USD, and map exposure to Ueno-linked Grupo Vázquez companies and to counterparties dependent on IPS or Caja Fiscal payments. (2) Contracts: index prices to the BCP planilla, add FX-adjustment and banking-holiday clauses, and shorten receivables where possible. (3) Supply chain: about 320 Brazilian firms with Paraguayan plants, 90 in textiles, face tighter credit; expect slower payments and more requests for supplier financing. (4) Energy-intensive projects: secure long-term PPAs before the 2027-28 supply crunch; ANDE's 286 MW Kuntur contract and the end-2027 crypto deadline show priority access is going to AI data centres, while tariffs are frozen for a year. (5) Telecom: Claro is live in 27 cities while Tigo and Personal must launch by February 2027; equipment, integration and data-centre opportunities exist, but the technical rules still exclude Chinese 5G vendors, so focus on non-RAN layers and enterprise solutions. (6) Public sector: expect delays and re-tendering at MOPC, MITIC and ANDE as the new government reviews contracts. (7) Political risk: Alliana governs with a fragmented Colorado Party and a mobilised street; continuity on Taiwan and the US is likely, but a Beijing opening cannot be excluded, so avoid making Taiwan-related commitments a condition of commercial deals.
